overview: An absolute rotary encoder reports the shaft's exact angular position as soon as power is applied, with no homing move required, because its internal disc or magnetic pattern encodes a unique code word for every distinct position rather than a repeating incremental pattern. That's the fundamental difference from a cheap incremental encoder: an incremental encoder only knows it moved N steps since power-on and loses that reference completely on a power cycle, while this one still knows exactly where the shaft is even after being unpowered and manually rotated. Industrial versions communicate over a synchronous serial interface (SSI) with RS-422 differential signaling rather than simple TTL, since they're built for long cable runs in electrically noisy machine environments. Multi-turn variants add a geared or Wiegand-effect turn counter so the encoder also remembers how many full revolutions have occurred, not just the angle within one turn.
simpleSummary: A sealed metal shaft encoder that always knows its exact angle the instant it's powered on, without ever needing to re-home.

specifications.resolution: 13-bit single-turn (8192 steps/revolution); optional 12-bit turns counter (4096 revolutions) on multi-turn models
specifications.interface: SSI (Synchronous Serial Interface), RS-422 differential clock and data
specifications.outputCode: Binary or Gray code, jumper/DIP selectable
specifications.maxClockFrequency: up to 2 MHz SSI clock at short cable length; typically derated to 300 kHz-1 MHz on longer industrial runs
specifications.shaftType: 6 mm solid shaft, radial or axial cable/connector exit

pinMap.name: V+
pinMap.function: Positive supply for the encoder's internal optics/magnetics and RS-422 line drivers.
pinMap.gotcha: The wide input range makes it tempting to wire straight into a hobbyist 5V rail out of habit — this device needs the higher industrial voltage and simply won't respond correctly (or at all) on logic-level power.

pinMap.name: CLK+
pinMap.function: SSI clock input, non-inverting — driven by the controller/PLC, not the encoder, to shift out position bits.
pinMap.gotcha: The encoder is purely a slave here; it never initiates a transfer on its own. If nothing toggles this clock line, the encoder sits idle even though it's powered and has a valid position.

pinMap.name: CLK-
pinMap.function: SSI clock input, inverting, paired with CLK+.
pinMap.gotcha: At cable runs beyond a few meters, the clock frequency must be reduced per the SSI cable-length/frequency chart or reflections corrupt data bits — that shows up as intermittently wrong positions, not a dead encoder.

pinMap.name: DATA+
pinMap.function: SSI data output, non-inverting — shifts out the current absolute position, MSB first, synchronized to CLK.
pinMap.gotcha: There's no explicit 'start' command like a UART frame — after all resolution bits are clocked out, most SSI encoders just repeat the last value until a clock-low period longer than the monoflop timeout (commonly ~20-40 microseconds) resets the frame for a fresh read.

pinMap.name: DATA-
pinMap.function: SSI data output, inverting, paired with DATA+.

pinMap.name: SHIELD
pinMap.function: Cable shield / drain, connected to the connector housing.
pinMap.gotcha: Ground this at one end only (the controller cabinet) — grounding both ends is a very common source of intermittent bit errors on long industrial cable runs.

useCases.title: Robot joint absolute position feedback
useCases.scenario: Mount on a joint so the controller knows exact joint angle immediately at power-on, skipping the homing routine that an incremental encoder would require.

useCases.title: CNC/gantry axis position feedback
useCases.scenario: Replace a limit-switch homing sequence with direct absolute position readout on power-up, saving cycle time on every machine start.

useCases.title: Crane/hoist load-height measurement
useCases.scenario: Track hoist drum rotation so the exact load height is retained through a power loss, rather than needing to re-reference to a known height after every restart.

useCases.title: AGV steering angle reference
useCases.scenario: Use a multi-turn absolute encoder on a steering column so the vehicle's steering angle is known immediately at startup without a re-centering maneuver.

useCases.title: Retrofit homing-elimination upgrade
useCases.scenario: Replace an incremental encoder plus limit-switch homing setup on an existing machine axis to cut startup time and remove a mechanical wear point.

commonlyPairedWith: Servo drive or motion controller with an SSI input card
oftenConfusedWith: Incremental rotary encoder (KY-040 style) — reports only relative step counts and completely loses its position reference on every power cycle, requiring a homing routine at startup, whereas this reports an exact absolute angle the instant power is applied
Optical wheel encoder — an open, unsealed hobbyist encoder disc not rated for the dust, vibration, or IP65 wash-down environments this industrial housing is built for
oftenUpgradedTo: Multi-turn absolute encoders with CANopen or EtherCAT fieldbus output, for direct network integration without a dedicated SSI interface card

beginnerMistakes: Assuming 'absolute' automatically means 'higher precision' than an incremental encoder — the real benefit is retaining position without homing, and resolution can actually be similar between the two types.
Wiring it like a hobbyist breakout on 5V logic without checking that it's actually a 10-30V device with RS-422 differential outputs, not TTL.
Skipping termination/proper differential wiring on long cable runs and getting garbled position data that looks like a sensor fault.
Mounting with a rigid, non-flexible coupling that transmits shaft misalignment stress directly into the encoder's bearings, causing premature failure.

Forgetting to configure the receiving controller's SSI bit count to match the encoder's actual resolution — a mismatched clock count reads the wrong bits as the most significant ones, producing a plausible-looking but wrong position.
